12.12 Solar Constant and Determination of Apparent Temperature of Sun
Solar constant is the solar radiation received per unit time by a unit area of a perfectly black
body placed at a distance of 1 astronomical unit from the sun. The area of a black body must
be normal to the radiation. It is denoted by S and its approximate value is 1361Wm-2. The
concept of a solar constant and Stefan's constant are used
to approximate the surface temperature of the sun.
